content: Your medications may interact with other drugs or increase the risk of severe side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use, including prescription, non-prescription drugs, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. In case of an overdose, if someone exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Laboratory and medical tests, such as blood counts, thyroid tests, viral levels, kidney and liver function tests, triglyceride levels, and eye exams, should be conducted before starting this medication and periodically during its use. Do not switch brands of interferon without consulting your doctor or pharmacist. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember, provided it is within two days of the scheduled dose. Resume your regular dosing schedule on the usual day. Store this medication in the refrigerator, away from light and moisture. Do not freeze it. Do not leave it out of the refrigerator for more than 24 hours. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Peginterferon alfa-2a is used alone or with other medications to treat chronic hepatitis B and C, viral infections of the liver. It works by reducing the amount of hepatitis virus in the body and enhancing the immune system's ability to fight the infection. It is not known if this medication can cure hepatitis B or C or prevent the transmission of the virus to others. Before using peginterferon alfa-2a, read the Medication Guide and Instructions for Use provided by your pharmacist. Consult your healthcare professional on how to prepare and use this medication. Inject it under the skin as directed by your doctor, usually once a week. The injection is typically administered in the abdomen or thigh, avoiding the belly button or waistline. Dosage is based on your medical condition, lab tests, and response to treatment. For a more comfortable injection, allow the medication to warm to room temperature as directed in the Instructions for Use. Do not warm it using other methods, such as microwaving or placing it in hot water. Do not shake the medication. Inspect the product for particles or discoloration before use; do not use it if either is present. Clean the injection site with rubbing alcohol before each dose. Rotate injection sites to minimize skin injury. Avoid rubbing the injection site after administration to reduce bruising. Use this medication regularly to achieve the most benefit. Many people experience flu-like symptoms, such as headache, fatigue, fever, chills, and muscle aches, which usually decrease after the first few weeks of treatment. These side effects can be minimized by injecting the medication at bedtime and using fever reducers or pain relievers like acetaminophen before each dose. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional guidance. Other side effects may include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, dry mouth, loss of appetite, dizziness, trouble sleeping, or redness/swelling at the injection site. Tooth and gum problems may also occur, sometimes worsened by dry mouth. Prevent dry mouth by drinking plenty of water or using a saliva substitute. Brush your teeth thoroughly at least twice a day and schedule regular dental exams. Temporary hair loss may occur. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. However, it may cause serious mental or mood changes, which could worsen during treatment or after the last dose. It may also weaken your immune system, increasing the risk of serious (rarely fatal) infections or worsening existing infections. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before using peginterferon alfa-2a, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, polyethylene glycol (PEG), or any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. This medication may increase your susceptibility to infections or worsen existing infections. Avoid contact with individuals who have contagious infections, such as chickenpox, COVID-19, measles, or the flu. Inform your healthcare professional that you are using peginterferon alfa-2a before receiving any immunizations or vaccinations. This drug may cause dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate dizziness. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Refrain from consuming alcoholic beverages. Children may be more sensitive to the side effects of this drug, particularly mental or mood changes, such as severe depression or suicidal thoughts/attempts. Peginterferon alfa-2a may also slow a child's growth, potentially resulting in a lower final adult height than expected. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. You should not become pregnant while using peginterferon alfa-2a, as it may harm an unborn baby. Discuss reliable birth control methods with your doctor while using this medication. It is unknown if this drug passes into breast milk.
